questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from George Eliot's 1857 short story "The Sad Fortunes of the Rev. Amos Barton." Mr. Ely is a clergyman in the town of Milby.

By the laity of Milby and its neighbourhood [Mr. Ely] was regarded as a man of quite remarkable powers and learning, who must make a considerable sensation in London pulpits and drawing-rooms on his occasional visit to the metropolis; and by his brother clergy he was regarded as a discreet and agreeable fellow. Mr. Ely never got into a warm discussion; he suggested what might be thought, but rarely said what he thought himself; he never let either men or women see that he was laughing at them, and he never gave any one an opportunity of laughing at him.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It shows that Mr. Ely had originally been held in high regard by his friends and then details the events that caused their regard for him to subside.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It highlights the disparity between Mr. Ely's public and private behavior and then conveys why he labors to obscure his true self from other people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It implies that Mr. Ely's neighbors are more naive in their estimation of him than people in London are and then explains why his neighbors have been so easily misled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It presents the favorable opinion of Mr. Ely that other people hold and then describes the behaviors of Mr. Ely that enable him to maintain that favorable opinion.

explanation.short: Choice D: The text first reports other people's favorable opinion of Mr. Ely and then shows how his guarded conduct helps preserve it.
explanation.key_evidence: Others regard Mr. Ely as powerful, learned, discreet, and agreeable; he avoids heated disputes, hides his mockery, and gives no one an opening to mock him.
explanation.why_correct: The first sentence establishes Mr. Ely's favorable reputation among both laypeople and clergy. The next sentence lists the socially cautious behaviors—suggesting rather than declaring, concealing laughter, and avoiding ridicule—that enable him to keep that reputation. This two-part progression is exactly the structure described in choice D.
explanation.detailed: Track what each sentence does. The opening presents how two groups esteem Mr. Ely. The remainder does not narrate a fall from favor or compare Milby with London; it explains the tactful habits that protect his standing. Choice D therefore matches both halves of the text.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “It shows that Mr. Ely had originally been held in high regard by his friends and then details the events that caused their regard for him to subside.” — The text never says that anyone's regard subsides and recounts no events that damage his reputation.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “It highlights the disparity between Mr. Ely's public and private behavior and then conveys why he labors to obscure his true self from other people.” — The text describes Mr. Ely's guarded public conduct but neither contrasts it with private behavior nor states a motive to hide a true self.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “It implies that Mr. Ely's neighbors are more naive in their estimation of him than people in London are and then explains why his neighbors have been so easily misled.” — London is mentioned as a place where Milby residents imagine he would impress people, not as a group whose judgment is contrasted with his neighbors' judgment.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “It presents the favorable opinion of Mr. Ely that other people hold and then describes the behaviors of Mr. Ely that enable him to maintain that favorable opinion.” — The favorable opinions come first, followed by the behaviors that help Mr. Ely maintain those opinions.

questions.passage: Elio Sucena and colleagues have explored how convergent evolution—a phenomenon that occurs when the same trait evolves independently in two reproductively separate lineages—can result from a genetic mechanism shared by both lineages. Meanwhile, Patricia J. Wittkopp and colleagues have investigated how convergence occurs through different genetic mechanisms, but the relative prevalence of convergence through shared and different genetic processes is still poorly understood. This motivated biologists Delbert A. Green II and Cassandra G. Extavour to evaluate both types of convergence in a single study for their 2012 paper.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the overall structure of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It explains a widespread assumption about a phenomenon, describes two studies that are based on that assumption, and explains why the assumption is unfounded.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It discusses a particular study of a phenomenon, elaborates on how two other studies have approached this phenomenon in the past, and critiques the first study's approach.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It details the development of a field of scientific inquiry, gives examples of three studies that were important to this development, and speculates on how future studies can develop these ideas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It describes a phenomenon, provides examples of two studies of that phenomenon, and mentions a third study of that phenomenon.

explanation.short: Choice D: The text defines convergent evolution, summarizes two studies of it, and then introduces a third study that evaluates both forms together.
explanation.key_evidence: Sucena's team studied convergence through a shared genetic mechanism, Wittkopp's team studied convergence through different mechanisms, and Green and Extavour evaluated both types in one study.
explanation.why_correct: The passage moves through three clear steps: it describes convergent evolution, gives one study for each of two possible genetic routes, and notes that Green and Extavour conducted a third study covering both routes. Choice D reproduces that sequence without adding evaluation or prediction.
explanation.detailed: The passage is a compact survey, not an argument against an assumption. Its final sentence says the limited understanding of the two routes motivated Green and Extavour's 2012 study. Thus the structure is phenomenon, two examples, then a third study—choice D.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “It explains a widespread assumption about a phenomenon, describes two studies that are based on that assumption, and explains why the assumption is unfounded.” — No widespread assumption is introduced, and the passage never concludes that an assumption is unfounded.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “It discusses a particular study of a phenomenon, elaborates on how two other studies have approached this phenomenon in the past, and critiques the first study's approach.” — The Green and Extavour study appears last, not first, and the passage does not criticize its approach.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “It details the development of a field of scientific inquiry, gives examples of three studies that were important to this development, and speculates on how future studies can develop these ideas.” — The text does not trace the historical development of a field or speculate about future research.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “It describes a phenomenon, provides examples of two studies of that phenomenon, and mentions a third study of that phenomenon.” — It accurately follows the passage from the phenomenon to two earlier studies and then to a third study.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a translation of María Dueñas's 2009 novel The Time in Between. The narrator has just rented an apartment and is entering it for the first time.

Over the years there have been many times when my destiny has delivered me unexpected moments, unforeseen twists and turns that I've had to handle on the fly as they appeared. Occasionally I was ready for them; very often I wasn't. Never, however, was I so aware of entering a new stage as I was that afternoon in October when I finally dared to cross the threshold and my steps sounded hollowly in the unfurnished apartment. Behind me was a complicated past, and in front of me, like an omen, I could see a space opening out, a great empty space that time would take care of filling up.

©2009 by María Dueñas. Translation ©2011 by Daniel Hahn.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The narrator feels optimistic about the future success of a new business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The narrator recognizes that a particular moment marks a major shift in her life.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The narrator has always had a plan for how to handle big moments in her life.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The narrator wants to express her gratitude for the people who have helped her.

explanation.short: Choice B: Entering the apartment makes the narrator unusually conscious that one phase of her life is ending and another is beginning.
explanation.key_evidence: She is “so aware of entering a new stage” and sees a complicated past behind her and an empty space that the future will fill before her.
explanation.why_correct: The passage makes the threshold both literal and symbolic: as the narrator crosses into the empty apartment, she explicitly recognizes a new stage and contrasts her past with the open future. That recognition of a life transition is the central idea expressed by choice B.
explanation.detailed: The paragraph reflects on unexpected turns in the narrator's life, then singles out this apartment entry as the moment when she most clearly senses change. The past-behind and future-before imagery confirms that the focus is a major shift in her life, not a business plan or gratitude toward others.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “The narrator feels optimistic about the future success of a new business.” — No business is mentioned, and the open future is not described specifically as commercial success.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “The narrator recognizes that a particular moment marks a major shift in her life.” — The narrator directly identifies the moment as entry into a new stage and frames it between past and future.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “The narrator has always had a plan for how to handle big moments in her life.” — She says she often was not ready for unforeseen events, which contradicts the claim that she always had a plan.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “The narrator wants to express her gratitude for the people who have helped her.” — The paragraph names no helpers and expresses no gratitude; its focus is the narrator's awareness of transition.

choices.label: B

explanation.key_evidence: The T-38's streamlined nose reduces wind resistance, whereas the boxy semitruck encounters more wind resistance.
explanation.why_correct: The final sentence switches from an example of aerodynamic design to an opposing example of bulky design. “On the other hand” precisely signals that contrast, so choice D creates the logical connection.

choice_analysis.D: Correct. “On the other hand,” — It accurately signals the opposition between the sleek jet and the boxy semitruck.

questions.passage: In astrophysics, a ring of debris orbiting a larger object within the object's Roche limit is expected to persist as a ring, whereas a ring of debris orbiting outside this limit would likely accrete into a satellite (e.g., a moon). Bruno Morgado and colleagues, ______ detected a dense ring of material orbiting the trans-Neptunian object Quaoar at a distance of 2,500 miles, well outside the calculated Roche limit of 1,100 miles, that has remained intact.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: fittingly,

choices.label: B
choices.text: for example,

choices.label: C
choices.text: likewise,

choices.label: D
choices.text: though,

explanation.short: Choice D: “Though” signals that Quaoar's intact ring is an exception to the expectation for debris beyond the Roche limit.
explanation.key_evidence: Rings outside the Roche limit are expected to form satellites, but Quaoar's ring remains intact at 2,500 miles—well beyond its 1,100-mile limit.
explanation.why_correct: The observation conflicts with the rule stated in the first sentence. Used parenthetically after “Morgado and colleagues,” “though” introduces this unexpected counterexample, making choice D the logical transition.
explanation.detailed: The first sentence creates an expectation; the second reports evidence that violates it. A concessive transition is therefore needed. “Though” marks the exception, while the other choices would suggest agreement, illustration, or similarity.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “fittingly,” — “Fittingly” would indicate that the finding matches the expectation, but the intact outer ring contradicts it.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “for example,” — “For example” would present Quaoar as an instance of the rule, although it is an exception to that rule.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “likewise,” — “Likewise” signals similarity to the expected pattern, not the observed contradiction.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “though,” — It correctly marks the intact ring as a surprising exception to the Roche-limit expectation.

Evidence that unstable power undermines wireless communication establishes that need. The alternatives either weaken the CFRP claim, contradict compatibility, or address sufficiency without proving the necessity of steadiness.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “The near-constant kinetic vibration of a spacecraft makes it possible to power its wireless communication devices using only non-CFRP piezoelectric harvesters.” — Successful use of non-CFRP harvesters would not establish that the new CFRP design's steady output is the required feature.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “Intermittent or unpredictable electrical supply undermines the efficacy of wireless communication devices.” — It directly explains why intermittent output is unacceptable and steady output is a prerequisite.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “The CFRP electrode is incompatible with most wireless communication devices.” — Incompatibility with most devices would undermine rather than support the claim about powering them.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “The high conductivity of the CFRP is what makes the energy output from a piezoelectric harvester sufficient for wireless communication devices.” — It attributes sufficient output to conductivity but does not show why a steady load is necessary for wireless communication.

questions.passage: Consumers increasingly expect that goods they purchase online will be delivered rapidly, even as soon as the day of purchase. Although efficiencies in long-distance transport of parcels have greatly improved delivery times, last-mile logistics (the final step in delivery to consumers) present a bottleneck for delivery companies. Time pressure resulting from consumer expectations is not the only challenge; other obstacles, such as the increasing congestion of roadways, persist. While innovations to mitigate these challenges have been emerging—the use of aerial drones, for instance—success has been constrained due to the additional complications that arise (e.g., a lack of suitable drone landing sites in residential areas). Consequently, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: in the near term, delivery companies are unlikely to overcome the impediments associated with last-mile logistics.

choices.label: B
choices.text: innovations in last-mile logistics seem poised to increase consumers' expectations for rapid delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: delivery companies should invest more funds in proven long-distance transport technologies than in untested last-mile solutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the use of aerial drones may enable delivery companies to meet consumers' expectations now but likely is not viable as a permanent solution.

explanation.short: Choice A: Persistent last-mile obstacles and complications that limit new solutions make a near-term resolution unlikely.
explanation.key_evidence: Road congestion persists, and even emerging solutions such as aerial drones are constrained by added complications like the lack of residential landing sites.
explanation.why_correct: The passage accumulates reasons that last-mile logistics remain difficult and then uses “Consequently” to request the result of those reasons. The supported result is that companies are unlikely to overcome the impediments soon, as choice A states.
explanation.detailed: Long-distance transport has improved, but the final delivery step remains a bottleneck. Time pressure, congestion, and limitations on proposed innovations all point to continued near-term difficulty. They do not support a prediction of rising expectations, a spending recommendation, or present success for drones.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. “in the near term, delivery companies are unlikely to overcome the impediments associated with last-mile logistics.” — It is the logical consequence of persistent obstacles and constrained attempted solutions.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “innovations in last-mile logistics seem poised to increase consumers' expectations for rapid delivery.” — The passage says consumer expectations create pressure; it does not say logistics innovations will increase those expectations.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “delivery companies should invest more funds in proven long-distance transport technologies than in untested last-mile solutions.” — No evidence compares investment returns or recommends shifting funds back to long-distance transport.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “the use of aerial drones may enable delivery companies to meet consumers' expectations now but likely is not viable as a permanent solution.” — The text says drone success is already constrained, so it does not establish that drones can meet expectations now.

questions.passage: Scientists looking for signs of ancient life in Asia have found many examples of fossilized hominins, including in a geological formation at the Minatogawa Limestone Quarry. However, to find even older specimens like early multicellular organisms from the Ediacaran period, scientists must look elsewhere, such as in the Ediacaran geological formation at Mistaken Point in North America, because ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: North America has sites with hominins but not sites with early multicellular organisms.

choices.label: B
choices.text: early multicellular organisms are found at more sites around the world than hominins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: that formation is from an earlier time than the formation with the hominins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the hominins at Mistaken Point are better preserved than the hominins at the Minatogawa Limestone Quarry.

explanation.short: Choice C: Scientists must use the Mistaken Point formation because it is older than the formation containing the hominin fossils.
explanation.key_evidence: The target specimens are older Ediacaran multicellular organisms, so researchers must examine an Ediacaran formation rather than the later formation containing hominins.
explanation.why_correct: The passage's word “because” requires a reason that connects geological age to the search location. Choice C supplies that reason: the Mistaken Point formation dates to an earlier time and can therefore contain the older organisms sought.
explanation.detailed: The contrast is chronological, not about continent-wide abundance or preservation. Minatogawa yields hominins, while the earlier Mistaken Point formation is appropriate for Ediacaran organisms. Choice C completes that age-based logic.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “North America has sites with hominins but not sites with early multicellular organisms.” — The passage expressly identifies Mistaken Point in North America as a site for early multicellular organisms, so this claim is false.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “early multicellular organisms are found at more sites around the world than hominins.” — The relative number of sites worldwide would not explain why this particular older formation is needed.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. “that formation is from an earlier time than the formation with the hominins.” — Its earlier geological age directly explains why scientists search there for older organisms.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “the hominins at Mistaken Point are better preserved than the hominins at the Minatogawa Limestone Quarry.” — The passage does not place hominins at Mistaken Point or compare their preservation.

questions.passage: Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) capitalize on the ability of some species of bacteria to metabolize metal, liberating electrons. The bacteria form a dense biofilm on the surface of an electron-collecting anode, but moving the electrons from the bacterial cytoplasm to an external electrode requires that the electrons pass through a series of inefficient oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions. Accordingly, MFC power output rarely exceeds a density of 0.30 milliwatts per square centimeter (mW/cm²). In an experiment, researchers added silver nanoparticles to carbon paper covering the anode in an MFC. The resulting power density was 0.66 mW/cm². Since metals such as silver exhibit high electrical conductivity, the researchers hypothesized that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: silver nanoparticles may increase the metabolic processes of the bacteria, thereby increasing the number of free electrons available to transfer to the electrode.

choices.label: B
choices.text: as the density of the biofilm increases, the series of redox reactions may accelerate independent of the presence of the silver nanoparticles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: electrons may be conducted directly to the electrode before the silver nanoparticles catalyze the redox reactions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: silver nanoparticles may allow electrons to bypass the series of redox reactions and transfer directly to the electrode.

explanation.short: Choice D: Conductive silver could give electrons a direct path to the electrode that bypasses the inefficient redox sequence.
explanation.key_evidence: After conductive silver nanoparticles were added at the anode, power density rose from at most 0.30 to 0.66 mW/cm².
explanation.why_correct: The passage identifies the inefficient series of redox reactions between the bacterial cytoplasm and the electrode as the bottleneck. Because silver conducts electricity well and the silver-treated cell produced more power, the researchers could reasonably hypothesize that silver lets electrons bypass those reactions and reach the electrode directly.
explanation.detailed: The explanation must connect silver's conductivity to removal of the identified transfer bottleneck. Choice D does so. The other options shift the mechanism to metabolism or biofilm density, or describe direct transfer occurring before an unsupported catalytic step rather than through the silver pathway.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “silver nanoparticles may increase the metabolic processes of the bacteria, thereby increasing the number of free electrons available to transfer to the electrode.” — The passage attributes the possible improvement to electrical conductivity, not to faster bacterial metabolism or production of more electrons.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “as the density of the biofilm increases, the series of redox reactions may accelerate independent of the presence of the silver nanoparticles.” — Biofilm density was not the manipulated variable, and a faster redox sequence would not explain silver's proposed conductive role.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “electrons may be conducted directly to the electrode before the silver nanoparticles catalyze the redox reactions.” — It gives the sequence backward and invents a catalytic role: the proposed direct conduction would occur through the silver instead of redox reactions.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “silver nanoparticles may allow electrons to bypass the series of redox reactions and transfer directly to the electrode.” — It directly links silver's conductivity to a route around the inefficient redox reactions.

questions.passage: The ratio of methane to other atmospheric constituents—represented by a measure called the methane mole fraction—influences a variety of meteorological phenomena, notably precipitation and humidity. For Titan, Saturn's largest moon, the observational data that exist are too sparse and discrepant to fully constrain the range of the methane mole fraction at various atmospheric levels. Juan Lora and colleagues point out that outputs of the IPSL atmospheric model of Titan, which track closely to observations in some respects, reflect how the model's developers responded to this challenge: by prescribing a uniform methane mole fraction for the lowest level of the atmosphere. It is therefore important to note that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: further observations of Titan may clarify the moon's methane mole fraction sufficiently for the model to employ a single value rather than a range.

choices.label: B
choices.text: some disagreements between the model's simulations of Titan's precipitation and humidity and the moon's actual precipitation and humidity are to be expected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: inconsistencies across the model's simulations of Titan's precipitation and humidity could be attributable to variations in the moon's methane mole fraction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: even though the model's outputs sometimes agree with observational data, Titan's real methane mole fraction is likely higher than the methane mole fraction used in the model.

explanation.short: Choice B: A model that imposes one methane value despite sparse and discrepant real data can reasonably diverge from Titan's actual precipitation and humidity.
explanation.key_evidence: The IPSL model prescribes a uniform lowest-level methane mole fraction even though observations are too sparse and discrepant to constrain the real range.
explanation.why_correct: Methane mole fraction affects precipitation and humidity. Since the model simplifies an uncertain, possibly varying real quantity to one uniform value, some model-versus-observation disagreement in those phenomena is expected. Choice B states that limitation.
explanation.detailed: The phrase “It is therefore important to note” asks for a consequence of the modeling choice. The consequence is potential mismatch with reality, not inconsistency among simulations or proof that Titan's real methane value is higher. Choice B follows the evidence without adding a direction the data cannot establish.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “further observations of Titan may clarify the moon's methane mole fraction sufficiently for the model to employ a single value rather than a range.” — The model already uses a single value; better observations might reveal a range rather than justify continuing that simplification.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “some disagreements between the model's simulations of Titan's precipitation and humidity and the moon's actual precipitation and humidity are to be expected.” — It correctly identifies the expected model-versus-reality mismatch caused by an uncertain input fixed at one value.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “inconsistencies across the model's simulations of Titan's precipitation and humidity could be attributable to variations in the moon's methane mole fraction.” — Because the model prescribes a uniform value, the passage does not attribute variation across its own simulations to changing methane fractions.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “even though the model's outputs sometimes agree with observational data, Titan's real methane mole fraction is likely higher than the methane mole fraction used in the model.” — Sparse and discrepant observations do not establish that Titan's real methane fraction is specifically higher than the model's value.

questions.passage: Cy Twombly, a US painter and sculptor, created many large-scale abstract works, such as his 10-painting series Fifty Days at Iliam. In these works, Twombly's artistic style is exemplified by his use of graffiti-like ______ often incorporate words or phrases from poetry and mythology.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: scribbles. That

choices.label: B
choices.text: scribbles; that

choices.label: C
choices.text: scribbles: that

choices.label: D
choices.text: scribbles that

explanation.short: Choice D: The restrictive relative clause “that often incorporate words or phrases” must directly modify “scribbles” without intervening punctuation.
explanation.key_evidence: The complete phrase is “graffiti-like scribbles that often incorporate words or phrases from poetry and mythology.”
explanation.why_correct: The clause beginning with “that” identifies a characteristic of the plural noun “scribbles.” It is not an independent clause and should remain attached to its antecedent, so choice D correctly uses no punctuation.
explanation.detailed: A period or semicolon would leave “That often incorporate…” as a fragment. A colon is also inappropriate because the dependent relative clause directly modifies “scribbles” rather than functioning as a separately introduced explanation or list.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “scribbles. That” — The period makes “That often incorporate words or phrases…” a sentence fragment.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “scribbles; that” — A semicolon requires independent clauses on both sides, but the “that” clause is dependent.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “scribbles: that” — The colon unnecessarily breaks the noun away from its restrictive relative clause and does not introduce an independent explanation or list.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “scribbles that” — It correctly attaches the relative clause directly to the noun “scribbles.”

questions.passage: Kizomba, a genre of dance that originated in Angola, has become an international ______ 2022, the Indian dance duo known as Elvis and Namrata defeated performers from around the world to win the annual Olympiads of Kizomba competition held in Paris, France, becoming the first ever Asian winners.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: phenomenon in

choices.label: B
choices.text: phenomenon, in

choices.label: C
choices.text: phenomenon and in

choices.label: D
choices.text: phenomenon. In

explanation.short: Choice D: One complete sentence ends after “phenomenon,” and a second complete sentence begins with “In 2022.”
explanation.key_evidence: “Kizomba … has become an international phenomenon” and “In 2022, the Indian dance duo … defeated performers” are two independent clauses.
explanation.why_correct: Because both clauses can stand alone, a period may separate them. Choice D supplies that period and preserves the introductory time phrase “In 2022” at the start of the second sentence.
explanation.detailed: The first clause makes a general statement about Kizomba's international status; the next gives a dated example. Choice D marks that boundary cleanly. The alternatives either attach “in 2022” to the wrong clause, create a comma splice, or omit the comma needed before a coordinating conjunction joining independent clauses.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “phenomenon in” — It makes “in 2022” modify when Kizomba became a phenomenon and then uses a comma to launch a new subject and predicate improperly.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “phenomenon, in” — The comma after “phenomenon” leaves two independent clauses joined only by commas, creating a comma splice.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “phenomenon and in” — It joins two independent clauses with “and” but omits the comma required before the coordinating conjunction here.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “phenomenon. In” — The period correctly separates the two independent clauses, and “In 2022” properly opens the second.

questions.passage: The Austronesian language family comprises some 1,200 languages—including the ______ Tetum and Fijian, which are spoken by 800,000 and 640,000 speakers, respectively—and accounts for one-fifth of the world's languages, making it of keen interest to linguists like Diane Massam.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: languages,

choices.label: B
choices.text: languages:

choices.label: C
choices.text: languages

choices.label: D
choices.text: languages—

explanation.short: Choice C: No punctuation belongs between the category noun “languages” and the names Tetum and Fijian that identify examples of that category.
explanation.key_evidence: The sentence's core phrase is “including the languages Tetum and Fijian”; the following comma begins the nonessential clause “which are spoken…”
explanation.why_correct: Choice C supplies the unpunctuated word “languages.” This keeps “the languages Tetum and Fijian” together as one noun phrase. The comma already printed after “Fijian” correctly introduces the descriptive relative clause, and the surrounding em dashes mark the larger interruption.
explanation.detailed: Read the completed interruption as “including the languages Tetum and Fijian, which are spoken by 800,000 and 640,000 speakers, respectively.” Tetum and Fijian identify the languages directly, so a comma, colon, or dash after “languages” would insert an unjustified break. Choice C is the only seamless construction.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “languages,” — A comma would wrongly separate “languages” from the names Tetum and Fijian that identify them.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “languages:” — A colon cannot follow the incomplete phrase “including the languages” to introduce these names.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. “languages” — The unpunctuated word keeps the category noun directly connected to the named languages.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “languages—” — An em dash would create an unnecessary internal interruption in addition to the dashes already enclosing the larger phrase.

questions.passage: Although 2060 Chiron and 2008 FC76 are both classified as centaur objects—outer solar system bodies in unstable orbits—they exhibit striking differences in ______ object 2060 Chiron is considered an active centaur, showing sporadic comet-like activity (such as clouds of dust and gas on its surface), 2008 FC76, showing no such activity, is considered dormant.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: behavior; the

choices.label: B
choices.text: behavior. The

choices.label: C
choices.text: behavior, while the

choices.label: D
choices.text: behavior: while the

explanation.short: Choice D: The colon follows a complete clause and introduces the promised explanation of the behavioral differences. ‘While the object 2060 Chiron is considered active, 2008 FC76 ... is considered dormant’ is a valid dependent-clause-plus-main-clause structure.
explanation.key_evidence: …bodies in unstable orbits—they exhibit striking differences in ______ object 2060 Chiron is considered an active centaur, showing…
explanation.why_correct: The sentence first makes the complete general claim that the two centaurs exhibit different behavior. A colon then introduces the details that explain that claim. After the colon, ‘while’ correctly makes the Chiron clause dependent, and the clause about 2008 FC76 supplies the main clause. Choice D therefore marks both the explanatory boundary and the internal contrast accurately.
explanation.detailed: The words before the blank form a complete clause ending with the general idea ‘differences in behavior.’ What follows explains those differences by contrasting active Chiron with dormant 2008 FC76, so a colon is the correct boundary. Within that explanation, ‘while the object 2060 Chiron is considered active’ is a valid dependent clause followed by the independent clause about 2008 FC76. Choice C does not damage that internal while-clause structure; instead, its comma leaves the opening independent clause and the later independent clause connected only by a comma, creating a comma splice. Choice D replaces that comma with the colon that properly introduces the explanation.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “behavior; the” — The semicolon may follow the first independent clause, but the text after it joins ‘Chiron is considered ...’ and ‘2008 FC76 ... is considered dormant’ with only a comma. That is a comma splice.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “behavior. The” — The period correctly ends the first sentence, but the next sentence still places the independent Chiron clause and the independent 2008 FC76 clause next to each other with only a comma. The result is a comma splice.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “behavior, while the” — Within the later contrast, ‘while’ validly subordinates the Chiron clause, and ‘2008 FC76 … is considered dormant’ is the main clause. But the earlier clause ‘they exhibit striking differences in behavior’ is also independent. Choice C connects those independent structures with only a comma, creating a comma splice; the colon in choice D correctly introduces the full explanatory contrast.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “behavior: while the” — The colon follows a complete clause and introduces the promised explanation of the behavioral differences. ‘While the object 2060 Chiron is considered active, 2008 FC76 ... is considered dormant’ is a valid dependent-clause-plus-main-clause structure.

questions.passage: Mitochondrial genomes reproduce asexually, which should over time result in an accumulation of harmful mutations and a decline in mitochondrial functionality. However, nuclear genes are hypothesized to coevolve with the rate of mitochondrial decline, eliminating mutational erosion. Such a compensatory measure ______ the organelle's decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation of mitochondrial reproduction.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.label: A
choices.text: had counteracted

choices.label: B
choices.text: counteracted

choices.label: C
choices.text: counteracts

choices.label: D
choices.text: counteracting

explanation.short: Choice D: “Such a compensatory measure counteracting the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” uses “counteracting” as a participial modifier. This leaves “offers” as the main verb of the grammatical sentence.
explanation.key_evidence: Such a compensatory measure ______ the organelle's decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory…
explanation.why_correct: The sentence provides the controlling evidence: The core sentence is "Such a compensatory measure ... offers an evolutionary explanation." The words in the blank should describe the measure, so use the participle "counteracting." Each other choice creates a finite verb before the main verb "offers" without a conjunction or proper punctuation. In the completed sentence, choice D, “counteracting,” preserves the required clause, agreement, and punctuation structure.
explanation.detailed: Start with the cited evidence: Such a compensatory measure ______ the organelle's decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory… The sentence provides the controlling evidence: The core sentence is "Such a compensatory measure ... offers an evolutionary explanation." The words in the blank should describe the measure, so use the participle "counteracting." Each other choice creates a finite verb before the main verb "offers" without a conjunction or proper punctuation. In the completed sentence, choice D, “counteracting,” preserves the required clause, agreement, and punctuation structure. The most tempting alternative is choice A, but “Such a compensatory measure had counteracted the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” contains the finite verb “had counteracted” and then the additional finite verb “offers” with no valid connection.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “had counteracted” — “Such a compensatory measure had counteracted the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” contains the finite verb “had counteracted” and then the additional finite verb “offers” with no valid connection.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “counteracted” — “Such a compensatory measure counteracted the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” likewise creates two unconnected finite verbs, “counteracted” and “offers.”
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “counteracts” — “Such a compensatory measure counteracts the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” has the same run-on predicate problem: “counteracts” and “offers” cannot both serve as the main verb here.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “counteracting” — “Such a compensatory measure counteracting the organelle’s decline, unlike enzyme-stabilizing accessory proteins, offers an evolutionary explanation” uses “counteracting” as a participial modifier. This leaves “offers” as the main verb of the grammatical sentence.

questions.passage: In a US national election, one might expect major-party campaigns to focus on the most populous states. explanation.short: Choice D: Plural determine correctly completes the sentence.
explanation.key_evidence: Ultimately, a state's voting record and polling data, not its population size, ______ its importance to campaigns.
explanation.why_correct: The sentence provides the controlling evidence: the compound subject a state's voting record and polling data takes the plural verb determine. In the completed sentence, choice D, “determine,” preserves the required clause, agreement, and punctuation structure.
explanation.detailed: Start with the cited evidence: Ultimately, a state's voting record and polling data, not its population size, ______ its importance to campaigns. The sentence provides the controlling evidence: the compound subject a state's voting record and polling data takes the plural verb determine. In the completed sentence, choice D, “determine,” preserves the required clause, agreement, and punctuation structure. The most tempting alternative is choice A, but Singular determines disagrees with the compound subject.

questions.passage: To notice subtle variations in the progression of the still life painting genre in Europe, first consider Willem van Aelst's "Still Life with Dead Game" from 1661; ______ compare it to Jan van Huysum's "Still Life with Flowers" from 1723.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: therefore,

choices.label: B
choices.text: still,

choices.label: C
choices.text: instead,

choices.label: D
choices.text: next,

explanation.short: Choice D: “Next” marks the second step in the instruction: first consider one painting, then compare it with another.
explanation.key_evidence: The sentence explicitly begins the sequence with “first consider” and then asks the reader to perform the comparison.
explanation.why_correct: The text's two imperative clauses form an ordered procedure. “Next” is the transition that advances from the first observation to the second, so choice D makes the sequence clear.
explanation.detailed: The second action is neither a result, a concession, nor a replacement for the first action; it follows it. The pairing of “first” and “next” gives the sentence the intended chronological instructional order.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “therefore,” — “Therefore” signals a logical result, but comparing the second painting is the next step rather than a consequence proved by the first.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. “still,” — “Still” signals persistence or concession, neither of which relates the two instructions.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “instead,” — “Instead” would replace the first action, although the reader is meant to perform both actions in order.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. “next,” — It correctly marks the comparison as the step following “first consider.”

questions.passage: Soil polluted with iron (a heavy metal) is harmful to many plants and animals, but the plant species Limnocharis flava, or yellow velvetleaf, not only thrives in such conditions but also helps remediate them. As a metal hyperaccumulator, Limnocharis flava absorbs a large amount of iron and stores it safely in its roots and shoots; ______ iron concentrations in the soil decrease.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: specifically,

choices.label: B
choices.text: accordingly,

choices.label: C
choices.text: nevertheless,

choices.label: D
choices.text: In addition,

explanation.short: Choice B: Because the plant removes and stores iron, “accordingly” correctly introduces the resulting decrease in soil iron.
explanation.key_evidence: Limnocharis flava absorbs iron from polluted soil and stores it in its roots and shoots; the following clause reports that soil iron concentrations decrease.
explanation.why_correct: The second clause is a consequence of the first: iron leaves the soil because the plant takes it up. “Accordingly” expresses that cause-and-effect relationship, making choice B the logical transition.
explanation.detailed: The sentence does more than add or restate information. It explains how hyperaccumulation remediates soil: plant uptake leads to lower soil concentration. Choice B signals this result, whereas the other transitions would imply specification, contrast, or simple addition.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “specifically,” — “Specifically” introduces a detail or restatement, not the consequence of the plant's iron uptake.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “accordingly,” — It accurately signals that decreased soil iron results from the plant's absorption and storage.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “nevertheless,” — “Nevertheless” signals contrast, but the decrease follows naturally from the uptake rather than opposing it.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “In addition,” — “In addition” merely adds information and fails to show the causal connection between the clauses.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Today, more than twenty different national currencies are referred to as "dollars."

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Modularity of mind is the notion that the mind is at least partly composed of innate neural structures (modules) that perform fast, necessary tasks.
• 1983: cognitive scientist Jerry A. Fodor hypothesized that low-level cognitive systems (e.g., perception, language) are modular.
• In Fodorian modularity, high-level systems (e.g., reasoning) are not modular.
• 2003: cognitive scientist Peter Carruthers proposed the massive modularity hypothesis (MMH).
• MMH expands modularity to include all cognitive systems.
questions.prompt: The student wants to compare Fodor's hypothesis with Carruthers's. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In 2003, Carruthers proposed the massive modularity hypothesis, disagreeing with Fodor's earlier hypothesis that the mind is composed of innate neural structures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In considering some but not all cognitive systems modular, Fodorian modularity is not as expansive in its definition of modularity as MMH is.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hypotheses of Fodor and Carruthers differ in whether they consider low-level cognitive systems, such as perception and language, modular.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Following Fodor's 1983 hypothesis, Carruthers proposed that modularity of mind includes all cognitive systems.

explanation.short: Choice B: Fodor treats only low-level systems as modular, while Carruthers's MMH includes all cognitive systems, so MMH is broader.
explanation.key_evidence: Fodorian modularity excludes high-level systems such as reasoning; Carruthers's massive modularity hypothesis extends modularity to every cognitive system.
explanation.why_correct: The notes show that the requested comparison is about scope. Choice B directly contrasts Fodor's some-but-not-all view with Carruthers's all-systems view and accurately concludes that MMH is more expansive.
explanation.detailed: Both hypotheses allow modularity in low-level systems, so that is not where they differ. Their difference is whether high-level systems are included. Choice B makes that distinction explicitly; the alternatives mischaracterize Fodor or fail to state the comparison.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. “In 2003, Carruthers proposed the massive modularity hypothesis, disagreeing with Fodor's earlier hypothesis that the mind is composed of innate neural structures.” — Carruthers does not reject the general notion of innate modules; he expands their proposed scope, while Fodor limits modularity to low-level systems.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “In considering some but not all cognitive systems modular, Fodorian modularity is not as expansive in its definition of modularity as MMH is.” — It accurately and explicitly compares the limited Fodorian scope with the all-system scope of MMH.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. “The hypotheses of Fodor and Carruthers differ in whether they consider low-level cognitive systems, such as perception and language, modular.” — Both Fodor and Carruthers treat low-level systems as modular; they differ over high-level systems.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. “Following Fodor's 1983 hypothesis, Carruthers proposed that modularity of mind includes all cognitive systems.” — It reports the chronology and Carruthers's position but does not explicitly compare that position with Fodor's limited scope.
